name: Avi Srivastava
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Avi is an Assistant Professor in the Genome Regulation and Cell Signaling Program of the Ellen and Ronald Caplan Cancer Center at The Wistar Institute in Philadelphia, where he started his lab in September 2023. He also holds the title of Wistar Institute Assistant Professor of Genetics at the Perelman School of Medicine, University of Pennsylvania. He is a computational biologist whose research combines statistical machine learning, high-performance algorithms and functional genomics. His lab builds BenchDrop-seq and Bagpiper for isoform-resolved single-cell biology. Earlier, he co-developed widely used quantification tools (salmon, alevin, alevin-fry) and integration frameworks (Signac, Seurat v5). His work has appeared in Nature Methods, Nature Biotechnology, Cell, Genome Biology, Nucleic Acids Research and Bioinformatics. Before joining Wistar, Avi was a postdoctoral fellow with Rahul Satija at the New York Genome Center and NYU. He earned his Ph.D. in Computational Biology at Stony Brook University, advised by Rob Patro.
